summary: Iteration 12 (affiliate/referral) — backend (9 pytest cases) + frontend Playwright coverage of LandingPage prefill, register w/ fake code, /help referral-card, copy, unauth gating. 8/9 backend pass. 1 critical backend bug: legacy backfill in /api/auth/me is dead code — Pydantic default_factory regenerates referral_code every load so it never persists and returns a different code on each call.

critical.issue: Legacy backfill never runs. User.referral_code is declared `str = Field(default_factory=_generate_referral_code)` (non-Optional with default factory), so when a user document loaded from mongo lacks the field, Pydantic silently generates a fresh value. The `if not current_user.referral_code:` guard is therefore always False, the db.users.update_one(...) backfill is never executed, and every subsequent /auth/me call returns a DIFFERENT random code for the same user. Verified: 3 consecutive /auth/me calls on a legacy user returned ['TPRQMY4Z','XCPPZWIU','EEAPOQHS']. Direct mongo read after the call shows referral_code field still missing. Impact: legacy users can never reliably share a stable referral link; their /api/auth/me/referrals will also report total_referred=0 because no one is `referred_by` an ephemeral code.

action_items: Fix legacy backfill in /api/auth/me. Recommended approach: change `referral_code: str = Field(default_factory=_generate_referral_code)` to `referral_code: Optional[str] = None` on the User model, and explicitly populate it in the register endpoint (and in get_me when missing). Then the `if not current_user.referral_code` check inside get_me will actually trigger the update_one. Alternative: in get_me, read the raw mongo doc first (without Pydantic) and check `doc.get('referral_code')` before constructing the User. After fix, retest TestLegacyBackfill::test_backfill_on_me — it currently asserts the field is persisted post-call.
critical_code_review_comments: User.referral_code field uses a default_factory but is non-Optional — this is the root cause of the silent backfill failure and a common Pydantic+Mongo pitfall.

Same Pydantic pitfall pattern: any future field added with default_factory will exhibit identical ‘phantom backfill’ behavior. Consider documenting a convention (Optional[X]=None + explicit assignment) for fields that are intended to be persisted-on-first-write.

rca of the issue: Root cause: Pydantic v2 `Field(default_factory=...)` on a non-Optional field always materializes a value at model construction. When a legacy mongo document missing `referral_code` is loaded via `User(**doc)` in get_me(), the factory fires and gives `current_user.referral_code` a fresh random value. The subsequent `if not current_user.referral_code:` check is therefore vacuously False and the `db.users.update_one({...}, {'$set': {'referral_code': ...}})` line is never reached. Reproduction: register user → mongo `$unset` referral_code → call /api/auth/me three times → returns three different 8-char codes; mongo doc still missing the field. Mitigation: either (a) `referral_code: Optional[str] = None` on User and explicitly set it in /register + on first /me read, or (b) bypass Pydantic for the raw read in get_me to inspect the actual stored value before deciding to backfill.
